slides.heading: WHY IT MATTERS
bullets: Waveforms and scopes show the truth about your image.
The RGB parade shows color balance.

slides.heading: SCOPE LAYOUT
slides.caption: The vectorscope shows hue and saturation—especially the skin tone line on the yellow-red axis.

slides.heading: WORKFLOW
steps: Read the waveform for exposure—skin sits ~50–70 IRE on Rec.709.
Check the parade for RGB balance on neutrals.
Use the vectorscope—keep skin on the skin tone line.
Calibrate your monitor annually—scopes do not lie.

slides.heading: PRO TIP
slides.text: Histogram alone lies on LOG—use the waveform for exposure.

slides.heading: COMMON MISTAKE
slides.text: Grading by eye on an uncalibrated display.
